messages:
Jorge (Customer Success): FYI we're getting a customer escalation: their rerank calls intermittently 500 when their documents contain emojis or weird bytes. Said it started after they bulk-imported chat logs.

Ava (Support): Can you paste the failing request/payload? any error from the API?

Jorge (Customer Success): Here's the minimal repro payload they sent (redacted):

```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query": "Which answer is best? 🤖\u0000", "candidates": ["Option A", "Option B\ud83d\ude0a"]}
```

Customer reports server sometimes returns 500 with body: `{"error":"internal error: invalid UTF-8 sequence in model input"}`. Other times it's a 400: `invalid utf-8 in request body`. They also saw `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 12: invalid start byte` in their app logs.

Ava (Support): Thanks. Do they see this consistently for the same message or only occasionally?

Jorge (Customer Success): Mostly when their ingest pipeline keeps null bytes or when they have surrogate halves from bad encoding. They said Node-based clients sometimes succeed but Python clients fail more often. They attached a full dump showing null bytes (`\u0000`) and some mojibake sequences.

Ken (Eng Oncall): Paging @Priya (Runtime) — seems like an input decoding edgecase hitting the rerank input path (continuous batching + prefix cache). Could be a library-level JSON decoder difference or our input sanitation.

Priya (Runtime): I'll pull the runtime logs. Can you paste the exact thread_ts for a failing request (from customer logs)?

Jorge (Customer Success): They gave us a sample request ts: 2026-03-10T18:12:07Z (we'll map to our logs).

infra-bot: Retrieved request id 7b9f3c2a for 2026-03-10T18:12:07Z, routed to runtime-pool-4.

Priya (Runtime): Found the request in logs. Runtime decoded JSON successfully then failed at tokenization:

```
[E] 18:12:07.432 decode.go:118: tokenize input failed: invalid continuation byte (0x80) at pos 14
[E] 18:12:07.432 request.go:220: request 7b9f3c2a -> model-run error: model input contained invalid utf8
```

Priya (Runtime): The interesting bit: our front-end JSON decoder does not remove null bytes (\u0000). Upstream tokenizer (the model tokenizer) chokes on certain byte sequences and our fallback to Latin1/replace isn't being triggered inside the batching path. Also saw a couple of entries where the client sent `Content-Encoding: gzip` but body was raw (bad client), which made us attempt gzip decompress and yield garbage bytes.

Ken (Eng Oncall): So there are a few failure modes: 1) genuine invalid UTF-8 in the payload, 2) mismatched Content-Encoding, 3) surrogate halves like `\ud83d` without the pair. We need to surface better errors and a mitigation for customers.

Ava (Support): Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they can't afford the 500s. They can run a preprocessor but want recommended approach.

Priya (Runtime): Short-term recommended mitigation to give to customers: sanitize inputs before calling /v1/rerank. Replace NULs with U+FFFD or strip them, normalize surrogate pairs with JS/Python libraries, and ensure the request Content-Type is application/json and no bogus Content-Encoding header. Also recommend urlsafe base64-encoding large binary blobs instead of putting raw bytes in the field.

Ava (Support): Can we implement a defensive filter server-side to return 422 with clearer message instead of 500? e.g., `422 Unprocessable Entity: invalid unicode in field candidates[2]`

Priya (Runtime): Agree. Filing a short patch to validate UTF-8 earlier in the pipeline and emit 422 with a pointer to the offending field. It should be safe to do in the API ingress; won't impact latency much. Will also add a warn-level counter for how many times we see NUL bytes or invalid sequences per minute.

Ken (Eng Oncall): Two follow-ups: 1) add a note in docs /best-practices about encoding and surrogate pairs, with example prefilter snippets for Python/Node; 2) add an automated sanitizer option at account level (opt-in) that strips disallowed characters before rerank batching.

Jorge (Customer Success): Customer asked for a quick repro we can give them in Python to demonstrate the failure and the workaround. Ava, can you post a small repro and a suggested sanitizer?

Ava (Support): Quick repro (Python):

```
import requests
payload = {"query": "pick one\udc00", "candidates": ["A\x00B", "C\ud83d"]}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', json=payload, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'})
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

Workaround sanitizer (Python):

```
def sanitize(s):
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        return s
    # replace NUL, fix surrogate halves, normalize
    s = s.replace('\x00', '\ufffd')
    import unicodedata
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)
    # drop lone surrogates
    s = ''.join(ch for ch in s if not (0xD800 <= ord(ch) <= 0xDFFF))
    return s
```

Ava (Support): Tell them to run sanitize on query and candidate strings before sending.

Priya (Runtime): We'll roll the ingress validation patch to staging in the next 2 hours. If it looks good we'll promote to prod with a stealth rollout (10% traffic) and alert counters.

Ken (Eng Oncall): If ingress returns 422 with a helpful error we should update SDKs to map that into a user-facing error class (InvalidEncodingError) so customers can auto-retry after cleaning inputs. Add to backlog.

Jorge (Customer Success): Customer is happy with the suggested workaround and asked for ETA on patch + whether we can retroactively identify affected requests to offer a sanitized replay.

Priya (Runtime): ETA: patch -> staging in ~2h, prod rollout later today if no regressions. We can query logs for requests with request-id prefixes and list candidates with NUL or non-utf8 bytes; but we can't alter customer data server-side without consent. Offer to provide a report of affected request-ids and counts.

Ava (Support): I'll send the customer the sanitizer snippet + offer for the report and a temporary mitigation checklist.

Ken (Eng Oncall): I'll take the SDK mapping ticket and the docs task. Priya, can you add the logging + 422 patch PR link here when it's up?

Priya (Runtime): PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/5543 — ingress utf8 validation + 422 response. Tests and integration checks included. Rolling to staging now.

Jorge (Customer Success): Thanks everyone. Customer wants to be notified when staging roll is up so they can test. I'll follow up with them and close once we confirm the prod rollout. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy staging/ingress-utf8-5543 started at 2026-03-11T12:02:00Z

Priya (Runtime): Staging pass looks clean; counters show 23 unique requests with NULs in the last 24h. Putting canary at 10% in prod now.

Ava (Support): Sending the workaround + repro now. I'll update this thread with customer feedback and attach logs if they consent.

Jorge (Customer Success): Closing the escalation for now pending prod canary success. Will reopen if customer still sees 500s after patch.
